title: AES-128 Bit faults: one-byte recovery (2 outputs) (Giraud, AES2004 proceedings published 2005)

target.description: Full AES-128; identify one 8-bit pre-final state value, hence one last-round-subkey byte through the correct ciphertext. Other key bytes remain outside this endpoint.

setting.key_relation: One fixed secret AES master key; no related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: Keys of the stated AES implementation without a weak-key restriction; fault protections are outside the model.
setting.plaintext_model: Repeat encryptions of the same plaintext under the same key; retain its correct ciphertext as a reference. Counts of faulty ciphertexts exclude that reusable reference unless explicitly stated otherwise.

fault_model.target: The state entering the final round, not a key-schedule fault.
fault_model.granularity: Exactly one bit is flipped in one state byte per useful execution.
fault_model.timing: Immediately before SubBytes in the final round 10, at state M^9.
fault_model.location: All counted outputs concern the same selected or postselected state byte; there is no whole-state coverage budget.
fault_model.value_control: The flipped bit is unknown; candidates cover the eight possible one-bit differences.
fault_model.sample_pairing: Every faulty output is matched to the same fixed-input correct reference; useful faults, random-location ciphertexts and physical executions have distinct accounting.

assumptions: The final AES round omits MixColumns; a single-bit state fault produces one nonzero output byte.
The reported outcome and data budget use the paper's candidate-filtering model; no numerical whole-key success rate is inferred from a byte-level statistic.

Appendix A uses random sets of thirteen wrong candidates among 255 values, with the correct value in every fourteen-element set. The printed probabilities belong to this set model, not a measured physical-fault distribution.

time.note: No numerical whole-endpoint runtime is reported for this version and endpoint.

data.note: All useful faults affect the same state byte, with unknown flipped bits; an additional correct ciphertext is reused.

memory.note: The article describes counters or candidate lists without a numerical peak-memory budget.

preprocessing.note: No separate reusable preprocessing-time budget is reported. The Appendix A 8×2^8 equation tests per useful output are a component count, not a complete attack cost.

success.description: Approximately 50% in the paper's random-set calculation. It is a local-byte theoretical estimate, not empirical or full-key success. Appendix random13-wrong-subset arithmetic independently reproduces0.4979575678/0.9666623475. Exact AES bit-mask sampling is a different model; no replacement success scalar is assigned. JMR07 separately reports71% one-byte uniqueness in software with2 random, repeat-allowed single-bit faults; retain this as a different later empirical event, not as a revised evaluation of the original random-subset formula. No trial denominator is supplied.

components.description: JMR07 author reprint PDF4 SectionIV-B.2/TableI straightforward-implementation row: software simulations report approximately71% unique recovery of ONE state/round-key byte after2 random single-bit faults, allowing repeated fault values. This concerns the original unprotected single-bit equation restated in SectionIII-A, not the scrambled/protected row. Trial denominator, success numerator, complete state/key sampling protocol and a uniform bit-mask law are not reported. It is a distinct later empirical model, not a replacement for Giraud's random13-false-subset estimate or a whole16-byte, master-key, physical-yield or native35-average/<50-budget success rate.

evidence.locator: Appendix A p.41 Eq.(33); Section 3 p.32
evidence.interpretation: Version-specific endpoint retaining its target, prior information, fault controls and native sample accounting.

evidence.locator: Complete proceedingsPDF1–15/printed27–41 and earlyPS15-page reading rendition; Sections3–6, AppendixA and references.
evidence.interpretation: Full exact-edition text and AES contribution inventory reviewed; component checks and whole-attack reproduction are separate.

evidence.locator: PDF2 SectionIII-A/Eq1; PDF4 SectionIV-B.2/TableI straightforward-implementation row.
evidence.interpretation: Later empirical one-byte recovery at the matching2-fault local count. Preserve primary0.5 from Giraud AppendixA's different random13-subset model; do not reassign it, create a same-population conflict, borrow the protected row, or infer joint last-round-key success. Exact experiment denominator and uniform bit-mask law are absent.

limitations: Useful faulty ciphertext counts do not automatically include ineffective physical injections or calibration attempts.
The article does not supply a measured success frequency, runtime or peak memory for every target and parameter choice.
